title: The The Distortion of Bhakti Value and Family Functional Crisis: A Social-Ecological Resilience Perspective on Narcotics Abuse among Balinese Women
abstract: Women’s involvement in narcotics offenses reflects the interaction of family dysfunction, cultural expectations, and socio-ecological vulnerability; among Balinese women, bhakti may become problematic when interpreted as unconditional obedience to male authority. This study aimed to examine socio-ecological risk factors, family dynamics, and distortions of bhakti contributing to narcotics abuse among Balinese women. A qualitative case study involved two incarcerated Balinese women selected purposively. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and thematically analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework and Ungar’s Social-Ecological Resilience Theory. The findings revealed two risk typologies. For the unmarried participant, narcotics use was associated with family conflict, paternal inconsistency, sibling influence, a permissive work environment, and escapist coping since adolescence. For the married participant, narcotics involvement emerged from a distorted interpretation of bhakti toward the husband, encouraging excessive obedience and codependent criminal involvement. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Integrating Islamic Values in English Language Learning: A Strategy for Faith and Character Formation
abstract: English learning in Islamic higher education should develop language competence while strengthening students’ faith and character; however, current practices remain focused on linguistic and cognitive outcomes, leaving Islamic values insufficiently integrated in a systematic manner. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an instructional strategy that systematically integrates Islamic values into English language learning to strengthen faith, character, motivation, and language competence. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model and a mixed-methods design. Participants consisted of one hundred forty-one undergraduate students involved in the needs analysis and students participating in three experimental groups during the implementation stage. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, classroom observations, documentation, pretest and posttest assessments, and student feedback instruments. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive analysis, validity and reliability testing, paired comparisons, and normalized gain analysis, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Implementation of Ethics Education in Elementary School from a Cultural Studies Perspective
abstract: Ethical education in elementary schools plays a crucial role in shaping students’ moral and social foundations, yet its implementation faces increasing challenges amid rapid social and digital changes. This study aims to analyze how ethical education is practiced, negotiated, and internalized through habituation, parental involvement, and the integration of local cultural values. A qualitative case study was conducted using data from teachers and school principals as research informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, document analysis, and limited classroom observations. The findings reveal that ethical education is not formally structured as a distinct curriculum component but is practiced through daily habituation, including morning greetings, collective prayers, classroom responsibilities, and communal activities. Verbal bullying and the influence of digital culture emerged as important challenges to students’ ethical development. The findings further indicate that ethical education operates as a negotiated social process through continuous interaction, classroom dialogue, and shared agreements between teachers and students regarding acceptable behavior. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Contextualizing EFL Learning Through Timor Tengah Selatan Culture: Its Contribution to Character Education at the Senior High School Level
abstract: EFL learning in senior high schools often remains disconnected from students’ local cultural contexts, limiting engagement and contextual meaning-making, while character education is frequently treated as an additional moral message rather than an integral part of authentic language tasks. Therefore, this study aims to analyze how Timor Tengah Selatan culture is embedded in genre-based EFL learning and to evaluate how this contextualization contributes to students’ character development. This study used a qualitative descriptive design. Data were collected through classroom observation, semi-structured interviews, and document analysis involving two English teachers and 30 eleventh-grade students. The data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The findings show that Timor Tengah Selatan culture served as authentic content across descriptive, recount, procedure, report, narrative, and speaking-performance activities. Teachers adapted topics, materials, tasks, and classroom interaction to connect English learning with students’ sociocultural knowledge. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Family Prophetic Education Indicators: Building Children’s Character in the Digital Age
abstract: Rapid digital transformation has changed family parenting patterns and posed serious challenges in shaping children's character and morals. The absence of measurable and validated indicators for prophetic values-based character education makes it difficult to systematically evaluate parenting practices in the digital age. This study aims to develop, test, and validate indicators of Family Prophetic Education (FPE) as a framework for strengthening children's character in the digital age. The study uses a research and development (R&D) approach with the Borg and Gall model. The research subjects involved 215 Muslim parents as empirical test respondents. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire developed based on literature review and validated by experts. Data analysis was performed using Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) to assess construct validity and Cronbach's alpha to test the reliability of the instrument. The results showed that 34 FPE indicators were valid and reliable, distributed across three main dimensions: transcendence (tauhid), humanization (amar ma'ruf), and liberation (nahi munkar), with a good model fit index (CFI = 0.91; RMSEA = 0.065; α = 0.954).

journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Revitalizing Local Folklore Values in Digital Fantasy Comics for Character Education
abstract: Literature learning in schools still faced the problem of low integration of character education and limited utilization of digital media that suited the characteristics of digital generation students. In addition, local wisdom values in traditional literary works had not been optimally utilized as contextual and meaningful learning resources. This study aimed to develop digital comic-based fantasy story teaching materials that integrated character values through adaptations of folk tales as an effort to strengthen character education. This study involved four expert validators consisting of material, language, presentation, and graphics experts. Data were collected using a validation sheet that assessed the appropriateness of content, language, presentation, and visual aspects. Data were analyzed descriptively and quantitatively using a Likert scale to determine the level of product validity, as well as qualitatively to formulate suggestions for improvement. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Enhancing Balinese Language Skills and Character Development in Early Childhood through Gending rare
abstract: The declining use of the Balinese regional language among young children indicates weakening transmission of local cultural values in everyday life. Increasing exposure to the Indonesian language and digital content has reduced children’s interaction using the Balinese language and traditional songs within family and school environments. This study aims to analyze the role of gending rare in strengthening cultural literacy, the use of the Balinese language, and character education in early childhood. A qualitative approach with an ethnographic design was employed, involving 2 children aged 5–8 years, 2 parents, 2 teachers, 1 school principal, and 1 school staff member selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, video documentation, questionnaires, and reflective journals, then analyzed through domain, taxonomic, componential, and cultural theme analysis using QDA Miner Lite. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Evaluation of the Religious Development Program at Juveniles Correctional Center
abstract: Religious guidance programs for adolescents in conflict with the law need to be evaluated to ensure their alignment with spiritual needs, character development, and social reintegration. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of religious guidance programs using the CIPP model (Context, Input, Process, Product). The study employs a mixed-methods approach with an evaluative case study design. The research subjects consisted of four informants: a religious counselor, a correctional facility staff member, and two youth in the program. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and document reviews, then analyzed descriptively based on the CIPP components. The results indicate that the program’s objectives align with the needs of the youth, particularly in strengthening religious practice, character development, and readiness for social reintegration. Resources and facilities were deemed adequate, but the curriculum was not yet standardized, and supervision was not yet optimal. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Teacher–Parent Collaboration through Digital Applications to Strengthen Self-Regulated Learning and Character Education in Elementary Schools: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Digital learning in elementary education, particularly in early elementary grades (Grades 1–3), requires the strengthening of students’ character development and self-regulated learning, as learners at this stage remain highly dependent on support from both family and school environments. This study aims to examine the roles of parental involvement and teacher–parent collaboration in fostering character education and self-regulated learning within digital learning contexts. This study employed a systematic literature review following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Literature searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for articles published between 2021 and 2025. The PRISMA process comprised four stages: identification (n = 53 records), screening (n = 45 after duplicate removal), eligibility (n = 38 full-text articles assessed), and inclusion (n = 24 studies included in the final synthesis). Thematic analysis, supported by a structured coding process, was conducted to identify recurring patterns across studies. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Picture Story Media Incorporating Pancasila Values to Improve Elementary School Students’ Reading Skills
abstract: Reading skills are fundamental abilities that support students’ success in understanding information and var-ious learning materials. However, elementary school students’ reading skills continue to face challenges, par-ticularly low reading interest and limited use of engaging and meaningful instructional media. This study aimed to analyze the effect of picture story media containing Pancasila values on elementary school students’ reading skills. The study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental method with a non-equivalent control group design. The participants were fourth-grade elementary school students divided into an experimental group and a control group based on the characteristics of the existing classes. Data were collected through a reading comprehension test measuring students’ ability to understand information, iden-tify main ideas, interpret text content, and draw conclusions, while the instrument was subjected to validity and reliability testing. The data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential analyses through a compara-tive test to examine differences in reading skills between the experimental and control groups. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Bibliometric Analysis of Local Wisdom-Based Character Education: Mapping Models and Learning Innovations
abstract: Research on local wisdom-based character education has grown substantially, yet its intellectual structure, thematic development, and research trends remain fragmented. This study aims to analyze the research performance, intellectual structure, thematic clusters, and emerging trends in local wisdom-based character education. A descriptive bibliometric approach was employed to analyze 94 Scopus-indexed journal articles published between 2017 and 2025. Data were collected from the Scopus database using a structured search strategy and analyzed with Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny through performance analysis, co-authorship analysis, co-citation analysis, and keyword co-occurrence analysis. The findings reveal a substantial increase in publications since 2020, with research productivity concentrated among several institutions and collaboration networks remaining relatively fragmented. The intellectual structure of the field is still developing, with studies drawing on diverse theoretical perspectives rather than a clearly established theoretical foundation. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Catur Paramitha as a Moral Foundation for Anti-Bullying Attitudes: Bridging Moral Knowing and Moral Feeling in Students
abstract: The high number of bullying cases among elementary school students shows that their moral understanding is not fully reflected in social behavior. This gap between moral knowledge and actions highlights the need for a character education approach that addresses cognitive, affective, and behavioral dimensions. This study analyzes the relationship between students' understanding of the Catur Paramitha values and their attitudes toward bullying. The study used a quantitative, correlational survey design with 140 students from SD N 2 Padangsambian, selected through total sampling. Data were collected using a validated and reliable Likert-scale questionnaire. Analysis utilized descriptive statistics and simple linear regression in SPSS. Results showed that students with a better understanding of Catur Paramitha values were more likely to reject bullying and show empathy toward victims. These findings suggest that local moral values influence not just cognition, but also social attitudes. The study concludes that systematic internalization of Catur Paramitha values can strengthen students' character and help prevent bullying. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Contribution of Social Sciences to the Formation of Elementary School Students' Attitudes in the Context of Character Education
abstract: This study examines how Social Studies (Ilmu Pengetahuan Sosial/IPS) learning contributes to the formation of elementary school students’ attitudes within the context of character education. Employing a qualitative descriptive case study, the research was conducted at SDN 2 Lambai, North Kolaka Regency, Indonesia. Data were collected through classroom observations, in-depth interviews with teachers, students, parents, and the school principal, as well as document analysis of lesson plans and school policies. Thematic analysis was used to explore the mechanisms through which character values are integrated into daily learning practices. The findings indicate that Social Studies learning facilitates the development of key character dimensions tolerance, cooperation, responsibility, honesty, nationalism, and empathy through contextualized instruction, experiential activities, teacher role modeling, and a supportive school culture. Values are not only introduced at a conceptual level but are practiced through group discussions, role-playing, socio-economic simulations, and routine school activities, resulting in observable patterns of self regulated and peer supported behavior. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Game Based Learning in Teaching Character Traits: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The increasing prevalence of behavioral problems among students indicates that character education continues to face challenges in fostering the meaningful and sustainable internalization of values. This condition highlights the need for more interactive and experiential learning approaches, one of which is Game Based Learning (GBL). This study aims to analyze the implementation of GBL in character education by identifying game types, design elements, character development mechanisms, character outcomes, and implementation challenges. The study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) using the PRISMA framework. Data were obtained through a systematic search of scholarly articles published between 2020 and 2025 and indexed in Google Scholar, Sinta, and Scopus, followed by screening based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The data were analyzed through descriptive synthesis to identify patterns and trends across the reviewed studies. The findings indicate that digital GBL dominates the literature, supported by interactive activities, adaptive personalization, and progression mechanics. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Transforming Character Learning through Digital Comic Media in the Era of Digital Literacyin elementary Schools
abstract: Character education in elementary schools faces challenges in the digital literacy era because conventional learning approaches have not fully accommodated students’ characteristics and digital experiences. This condition highlights the need for learning media that can integrate character development with engaging, contextual learning experiences aligned with the development of digital literacy. This study aims to analyze and explore the transformation of character education through digital comics and identify patterns of their integration with digital literacy in elementary schools. This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach by analyzing 30 relevant scientific articles published in national and international journals. Data were collected through literature searching, screening, classification, and information extraction based on predetermined inclusion criteria. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis and content analysis to identify patterns of findings and relationships among themes. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: PPI-Based Interactive E-Book: An Effective Solution for Building Environmental Awareness Among Science Students
abstract: The low level of environmental awareness in students' science lessons and the suboptimal use of Climate Change Education (PPI)-based teaching materials are the main issues in this study. This study aims to analyze a PPI-based e-book as a learning medium to improve environmental awareness and students' understanding of biodiversity material in fifth-grade elementary school. This research is a Research & Development (R&D) study using the ADDIE model. The research subjects included learning media experts and elementary school science material experts as validators, and 15 fifth-grade elementary school students as trial subjects. Data collection methods used questionnaires and objective tests. The results indicate that the developed PPI-based e-book has good quality in terms of appearance, content, and ease of use. This media is considered capable of encouraging active student engagement in learning, improving higher-order thinking skills such as analysis and evaluation, and fostering environmental awareness and behavior. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Reversed Value Internalization in Islamic Character Education for Students with Intellectual Disabilities
abstract: The internalization of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) values in inclusive education still tends to rely on cognitive approaches that are less suited to the learning characteristics of children with intellectual disabilities. This condition indicates a gap between character education theory and the actual process of Islamic character formation. This study aims to analyze the process of internalizing PAI values, explore the sequence of Islamic character formation, and formulate a contextual value internalization model for children with intellectual disabilities. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with a multisite case study design involving 12 participants, consisting of PAI teachers, school principals, parents, and students with mild intellectual disabilities. Data were collected through participatory observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews, and documentation studies using observation guidelines, interview protocols, and documentation sheets. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, which includes data condensation, data display, conclusion drawing and verification, as well as cross case analysis. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Interactive Flipbook-Based Indonesian Cultural Diversity Learning Media (KEBUDI) Incorporating Cultural Heritage for Pancasila Education
abstract: The use of technology-based learning media remains suboptimal despite adequate technological facilities in schools. Therefore, innovative and interactive media are needed to enhance students’ engagement in Pancasila Education. This study aimed to develop, analyze the feasibility, and examine the effectiveness of the Indonesian Cultural Diversity (KEBUDI) learning media in the form of an interactive flipbook containing cultural heritage to improve students’ learning motivation and learning outcomes. This study employed a research and development approach using the ADDIE model, involving experts, a teacher practitioner, and third-grade elementary school students as research subjects. Data were collected through interviews, questionnaires, and tests using interview guidelines, feasibility assessment sheets, and learning outcome test instruments. The data were analyzed using qualitative descriptive analysis, quantitative descriptive analysis, and inferential statistical analysis. The results indicated that the KEBUDI learning media based on an interactive flipbook containing cultural heritage met the feasibility criteria for use in Pancasila Education. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Andei-Andei of the Malay Jerieng Bangka Community as a Cultural Resource in Character Education
abstract: Oral literature is an important part of the intergenerational transmission of cultural values and character, but its use as a source of character education has not yet been studied in depth. This study aims to analyze the character education values contained in andei-andei a form of oral literature among the Jerieng Bangka Malay community and to explore its potential as a source of teaching materials based on local wisdom. The study employs a qualitative approach with an ethnographic design. The research subjects include andei-andei narrators and community members involved in the practice of transmitting this oral literature. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted using content analysis, interpreting the findings based on Lickona’s character education framework, which encompasses moral knowledge, moral feelings, and moral actions. The results indicate that andei-andei embodies six core character values: honesty, justice, willingness to help, compassion, cooperation, and courage, which represent the values of respect and responsibility. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Use of a Protractor to Improve Third-Grade Elementary Students’ Competence in Angle Measurement
abstract: The problem identified in the field was that 55% of students were already familiar with the protractor but remained confused about how to use it properly. This study aimed to determine the effect of using a protractor on improving third-grade elementary students’ competence in angle measurement. This study employed an experimental research method with a post-test-only control group design. The population consisted of 381 students. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, with 25 third-grade students in Class III A assigned to the experimental group and 28 students in Class III B assigned to the control group. Data on students’ angle measurement competence were collected using a 20-item multiple-choice test that had been validated. The data were analyzed using a t-test with pooled variance. The hypothesis testing results showed that t-count = 4.563 > t-table = 1.675, at a 5% significance level with degrees of freedom (df) = (n₁ + n₂) − 2 = (25+28)−2 = 51. The results indicated a significant difference in angle measurement competence between students who learned using a protractor and those who learned without using a protractor. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Innovation in Digital Information Literacy Learning for Generation Z through the FOSIL Model Perceptions
abstract: The rapid development of digital technology requires Generation Z students to possess not only technical skills but also critical and character-oriented digital information literacy. However, digital learning practices in schools tend to focus primarily on the use of technology, without a systematic inquiry framework to develop information evaluation skills and digital character formation. This study aims to analyze perceptions, readiness, and the potential adaptation of the Framework of Skills for Inquiry Learning (FOSIL) in digital information literacy learning. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving teachers, librarians, and students as research participants. Data were collected through semi structured interviews focusing on digital learning experiences, information-seeking habits, and perspectives on FOSIL implementation. The collected data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns, meanings, and interrelationships among the findings. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Enhancing Character Education and Students’ Positive Attitudes through Local Wisdom in the Era of Society 5.0: A Case Study in Vocational Schools
abstract: In the era of Society 5.0, education is no longer sufficient to focus solely on the mastery of technical competencies but is required to foster students’ character development in a holistic and sustainable manner. A major challenge faced by vocational education lies in integrating meaningful and contextual character education without neglecting cultural identity within an adaptive curricular framework. This study aims to explore and analyze the role of local wisdom as a foundation for character education and its contribution to shaping students’ attitudes and civic values through the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. This research adopts a qualitative approach with a case study design. The research subjects include teachers and students in vocational schools. Data were collected through participatory observation, semi-structured interviews, and document analysis. Data analysis was conducted using the interactive model of Miles and Huberman, encompassing data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Relationship Between Parenting Style and Independent Character Toward IPAS Learning Outcomes among Fifth-Grade Elementary School
abstract: Low IPAS learning outcomes, along with variations in parenting styles and students’ levels of independent character, indicate a problem that requires empirical investigation. This study aims to examine the relationship between parenting style and independent character on IPAS learning outcomes among fifth-grade students in the 2023/2024 academic year. The research employed an ex post facto design. The population consisted of 181 fifth-grade students, with a sample of 123 students selected through random sampling techniques. Data were collected using questionnaires to measure parenting style and students’ independent character, as well as documentation of IPAS Final Semester Examination (UAS) scores. The analysis results revealed that parenting style contributed 4.3%, independent character contributed 66.6%, and the combination of both variables contributed 68.5% to students’ IPAS learning outcomes. These findings indicate that independent character plays a more dominant role than parenting style in directly influencing IPAS learning outcomes, although both variables are interconnected. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Religious Moderation Education in Elementary Schools: Building Tolerance and Respect for Differences from an Early Age
abstract: The limited understanding and application of religious moderation values among elementary school students poses a significant challenge in fostering tolerant character from an early age. This study aims to analyze the implementation of religious moderation education within the elementary school curriculum and evaluate strategies used to cultivate tolerant attitudes. The research employs a library research method, with subjects comprising relevant literature, including scientific journals, books, and recent research reports indexed nationally and internationally. Data were collected through literature searches based on criteria of recency, thematic relevance, and source quality. Content analysis was applied to extract key themes related to the integration of moderation values in the curriculum, classroom practices, and teaching media. Thematic analysis revealed three main findings: (1) the integration of moderation values in the curriculum remains primarily normative; (2) classroom practices are influenced by limited teacher training and school policies; and (3) the lack of contextual teaching media hinders the internalization of values. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Tutulena: A Heritage Folk Game as the Foundation of Malind Cultural Character Formation
abstract: Character development has become a major concern due to the high incidence of bullying experienced by children, adolescents, and adults. Efforts to address this issue have been carried out through the implementation of innovative learning models and approaches grounded in local wisdom. This study aims to analyze the values embedded in the traditional folk game Tutulena as a means of character formation. The study employs a qualitative approach with research subjects that include children, adolescents, adults, and parents. Data were collected through documentation, interviews, and literature review, and subsequently analyzed using data triangulation. The findings indicate that Tutulena instills essential values such as cooperation, discipline, patience, perseverance, courage, sportsmanship, and cultural preservation. These values play a significant role in shaping positive character, as individuals learn to respect others, communicate effectively, and collaborate to achieve common goals through interactions in the game. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Two Pillars of Character Education: Harmony of Extracurricular Activities and School Culture
abstract: Character education requires an approach that can instill values deeply through habituation, role modeling, and real-life experiences, rather than through theory alone. This study aims to analyze the role of extracurricular activities and school culture as two main pillars in shaping student character. The research employed a qualitative approach using a literature study method. Data were collected from primary sources, including empirical research, secondary sources such as books and educational policy documents, and supporting sources from reliable media articles. Research instruments included a literature criteria checklist and a findings recording sheet, validated through expert review. Data analysis was conducted qualitatively through identification of main themes, concept classification, interpretation of relationships among concepts, and synthesis to achieve a comprehensive understanding. The results indicate that extracurricular activities such as Scouting, Red Cross Youth (PMR), and arts programs are effective in fostering responsibility, leadership, cooperation, and self-confidence through direct involvement. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Enhancing Religious Moderation through Islamic, Christian, and Buddhist Religious Subject in the Context of Character Education
abstract: The increasing symptoms of intolerance and exclusivism in educational settings have the potential to weaken social cohesion and hinder the formation of students’ national character. This condition indicates the need for pedagogical strategies that systematically instill the values of tolerance, justice, and respect for diversity within the learning process. This study aims to analyze and explore the strengthening of religious moderation through Islamic, Christian, and Buddhist religious instruction in heterogeneous school contexts. The research employed a qualitative approach with a phenomenological design involving religious education teachers and students as participants. Data were collected through classroom observations, in-depth interviews, and document analysis using structured guidelines, and were analyzed thematically through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing with triangulation to ensure validity. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Revitalizing the Character of Mutual Cooperation Based on Lotisan Culinary Tradition in History Learning Practices
abstract: Lotisan is a peripheral culinary tradition that holds significant value in maintaining social cohesion within Javanese rural communities. Amid the growing tendency toward individualism in modern life, integrating local wisdom into formal education remains a crucial challenge. This study aims to analyze the meaning of the lotisan culinary tradition from the perspective of Javanese society, examine its integration into history learning through demonstration methods in the topic of prehistoric human life, and evaluate its implications for the development of students’ cooperation character. This research employed a qualitative approach with a single case study design. Data were collected through non participant observation, in depth interviews, document analysis, and literature review. The participants included school leaders, history teachers, students, and community representatives selected through purposive sampling. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Effectiveness of Tri Hita Karana Based Digital Comics in Shaping Students' Global Diversity and Independence
abstract: Character formation at the elementary school level is a priority in the Indonesian education system however, its implementation remains less balanced compared to cognitive achievement. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of Tri Hita Karana based digital comic learning media in enhancing students’ global diversity and independence. The research employed a quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent post-test only control group. The participants were divided into two groups: an experimental group that used digital comics and a control group that received conventional instruction. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Integration of Reproductive Health Values in Islamic Religious Education Learning for Upper Elementary School Students
abstract: Reproductive health knowledge is a crucial element for improving individual quality of life and wellbeing, including among elementary school students. However, students’ understanding of this topic remains limited, putting them at risk of issues such as unintended pregnancy, sexually transmitted infections, and early marriage. This study aims to analyze strategies for integrating reproductive health values into Islamic Religious Education (IRE) learning for elementary school students. A descriptive-analytic qualitative method was employed, with data collected through interviews, observations, and document studies. Thematic analysis was conducted to identify patterns and integration strategies. The results indicate that integration is implemented through four main strategies: linking puberty with the concept of akil baligh, associating organ health with hifzh al-nafs, integrating risk behaviors with hifzh al-nasl and aurat, and connecting healthy communication with social etiquette. Effective learning methods include interactive lectures, storytelling, role play, and project based assignments. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Local Culture of Floating Market Traders in the Pancasila Economic Values
abstract: The transformation of local cultural values to the younger generation faces challenges due to the limited internalization of values in socio-economic practices. This study aims to explore and analyze local cultural values that develop in traders’ economic practices and examine their relevance as a medium for learning the Pancasila economic principles. This research employs a qualitative approach using an ethnographic method. The research subjects consist of traders as the main actors of economic activities, selected through the snowball sampling technique. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and documentation, with interview guidelines serving as the main research instrument. Data analysis was conducted through data condensation, data presentation, and drawing and verifying conclusions. The results show that traders’ economic practices reflect local cultural values aligned with the principles of the Pancasila economy, including barelaan, papadaan/bubuhan/badingsanakan, batutulungan, bakalah bamanang, ampun saorang, and honesty. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Cultivating Pawongan Values in an Eighth-Grade English Textbook English for Nusantara: A Strategy to Strengthen Character Education
abstract: Moral degradation influences the unstable relationship between humans. Maintaining a harmonious relationship among fellow humans is essential to avoid more serious problems. Therefore, the study aims to explore and present the Pawongan values in the eighth-grade junior high school textbook entitled English for Nusantara to recognize how the textbook involves character education development. The subject of the study was the content provided in the textbook, which means it is a content analysis research. The study utilised qualitative research procedures proposed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldana (2014). Data collection and analysis are conducted repeatedly and simultaneously through data collection, condensation, display, and conclusion drawing and verification. It was discovered that the Pawongan value is present in the home, school, and society. Pawongan values across those contexts internalize positive character development for students to be more respectful, sympathetic, empathetic, tolerant, solid, and equal. Therefore, the study shows that the concept of Pawongan in Tri Hita Karana contributes to character development through a local wisdom approach.

title: SPIRIT Model: Character Building Strategies in the Society 5.0 Era through the Integration of Tazkiyatun Nafs and Spiritual Growth
abstract: Learning in the Society 5.0 era still tends to prioritize cognitive achievement, while the strengthening of students’ character and spirituality has not yet been optimally implemented in school practice. This situation creates a gap between the demand to develop character that is adaptive to digital challenges and the limited availability of systematic, practical instructional strategies for instilling spiritual and moral values. This study aimed to develop and validate the SPIRIT Model (Spiritual Personal Improvement and Reflective Integrated Teaching) as a character-strengthening strategy by integrating the concepts of Tazkiyatun Nafs and the Spiritual Growth Framework (SGF). The research employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model and involved 38 teachers, 50 students, and 24 Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teachers. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and focus group discussions (FGDs). Three experts validated the model by assessing its content, presentation, syntax, and feasibility of implementation. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Internalization of Character Education in the Theatrical Work Segara Tanpa Tepi: A Study of Implementation in the Performing Arts
abstract: The development of the times and shifts in social values have led to a weakening of the internalization of character values in people's lives, especially among the younger generation. Based on this, the purpose of this study is to analyze the values of character education contained in the theatrical work Segara Tanpa Tepi. The approach used is a descriptive, qualitative method with an ethnographic approach. The subject of the study is the theatrical work [Segara Tanpa Tepi] as a medium for expressing Hindu character education values. Participants involved in this study were artists and spiritual figures. The selection of participants used a purposive sampling technique. The methods used for data collection included in-depth interviews, participant observation, and documentary studies. The research instruments were interview sheets, observation sheets, and documentation studies. The research data were analyzed using qualitative descriptive methods, following the steps of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Research Article An Analysis of Teachers’ Practices in Instilling Pancasila Student Profile Values through Local Wisdom
abstract: The internalization of the Pancasila Student Profile values represents a strategic step in shaping students’ character in line with the educational transformation promoted by the Merdeka Curriculum. However, challenges such as limited supporting facilities and learning approaches that are less contextual often hinder its implementation. This study aims to analyze teachers’ pedagogical practices in instilling the Pancasila Student Profile values through a local wisdom based approach. The research employs a descriptive qualitative approach with teachers as the primary subjects. Data were collected through participatory observation, in depth interviews, and document analysis, and were thematically analyzed to identify strategies, media, and the impact of integrating local wisdom into learning. Findings reveal that teachers actively utilize local cultural elements, such as mutual cooperation traditions, traditional games, and local legends, as a means of internalizing character values. The local culture based approach not only strengthens students’ understanding of Pancasila values but also enhances active participation and emotional engagement in the learning process. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Sorogan Method in Pesantren Education: Cognitive, Affective, and Psychomotor Learning Outcomes
abstract: The Sorogan method, as a traditional instructional model in pesantren, has rarely been examined systematically, particularly in relation to learning outcomes across cognitive, affective, and psychomotor domains. A key challenge is how this method can enhance academic competence, character development, and practical skills in a holistic manner. This study aims to analyze the contribution of the Sorogan method to the development of students’ academic abilities, character, and practical skills. The research employed a qualitative approach with a phenomenological design. Participants included active students, teachers (Mustahiq), and curriculum administrators. Data were collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and document analysis. Data analysis was conducted through stages of reduction, thematic categorization, and interpretative synthesis following phenomenological procedures. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: The Character in Transit: Rethinking Moral Education through Children’s Urban Experiences
abstract: The degradation of children’s character, such as declining discipline and responsibility, has become a major concern in primary education. Formal classroom learning is often considered ineffective in deeply internalizing moral values. This study aims to explore how elementary school students’ experiences in using mikrotrans public transportation contribute to character development. Employing a qualitative case study approach, the research involved seven participants, consisting of a school principal, a teacher, two parents, two mikrotrans drivers, and an education observer. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, documentation, and focus group discussions (FGDs), and analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. The findings reveal that experiences gained from using mikrotrans strengthen students’ character traits such as discipline, responsibility, independence, social awareness, tolerance, and communication. These findings highlight the urgency of expanding character education beyond classroom settings by integrating students’ daily mobility experiences as meaningful and contextual learning spaces. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Transcendental Humanist Character Paradigm: The Reactualization of Qur'anic Values Education in Islamic Education
abstract: Pedagogical practice is often trapped in a dichotomy between secular models that emphasize psychological and sociological aspects without a transcendent horizon and doctrinal models that demand normative obedience without honoring the humanity of learners. It is therefore necessary to reconsider a character education model that can integrate humanization and divine orientation, one of which is the humanist-transcendental paradigm proposed in this article. This study aims to: (1) explore the concept of the humanist-transcendental paradigm, (2) analyze Qur’anic values as its ethical and spiritual foundation, and (3) describe its implications for character formation in Islamic education. The method employed is library research. The findings indicate that, first, the humanist-transcendental paradigm conceptually combines the recognition of learners as dignified subjects with the linking of learning freedom to tawhid, adab, trustworthiness, ihsan, and God-consciousness through the teacher’s dual role as facilitator and role model. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Digitalisation and Its Impact on Family Values and Adolescents’ Emotional Health in Community Contexts
abstract: This study is grounded in the increasing use of digital technology, which has the potential to influence family values and adolescents’ emotional health in the context of social change. The study aims to analyze and examine the effect of digitalization on family values and adolescents’ emotional health. A quantitative approach with a survey design was employed. The research subjects consisted of 52 adolescents who actively use digital technology. Data were collected using a Likert scale questionnaire (1–5), each comprising 10 items for the variables of digitalization, family values, and adolescents’ emotional health. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, normality tests, and multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS. The results indicate that digitalization has a positive and significant effect on family values but does not have a significant effect on adolescents’ emotional health. These findings suggest that digital transformation has a greater impact on patterns of family relationships and interactions than on adolescents’ intrapersonal aspects. journal_name: Indonesian Values and Character Education Journal
title: Character Education-Oriented E-Module to Improve Learning Independence in Fourth-Grade Social Studies
abstract: The low level of students’ learning independence in Social Studies indicates the suboptimal integration of character values in the learning process and the limited availability of teaching materials that support independent learning. This study aims to develop and examine the effectiveness of a character oriented e-module in improving elementary school students’ learning independence. This research employed a research and development approach using the ADDIE model (analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation). The subjects of the study consisted of 34 fourth grade students. Data were collected through validation questionnaires completed by material and media experts, student response questionnaires, and a learning independence test instrument. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive quantitative and qualitative techniques as well as inferential statistical tests to determine the effectiveness of the developed product. The results showed that the developed e-module met the criteria of being highly feasible based on expert validation, received positive responses from students, and was significantly effective in enhancing learning independence.
